subject: english
question:
**A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.**

She said, "I am feeling cold."

options.text: She said she is feeling cold.
She said she was feeling cold.
She said she had felt cold.

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. She said she was feeling cold.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **direct speech**: "I am feeling cold."
 
• When converting direct speech to **indirect speech**, the tense of the verb changes depending on the reporting verb.
 
• Here, the reporting verb is in the past tense ("She said"), so the present continuous tense ("am feeling") in the direct speech changes to the past continuous tense ("was feeling") in the indirect speech.
 
• Thus, the correct transformation is: *"She said she was feeling cold."*

Correct sentence: *She said she was feeling cold.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for changing direct to indirect speech:**
 
 
• **Present Continuous → Past Continuous:** "I am feeling" → "She was feeling."
 
• **Present Simple → Past Simple:** "I feel" → "She felt."
 
• **Present Perfect → Past Perfect:** "I have felt" → "She had felt."
 
 
 
• **Example:** 
 
 
• Direct Speech: "I am working on a project."
 
• Indirect Speech: She said she was working on a project.
